chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal who said:

A man from the atheists asked me, saying, 'How did the zakat come to be twenty-five dirhams from every thousand?' So I said to him, 'Indeed that is like the salat — three [units], and two, and four.' He accepted it from me.

Then I met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) after that. So I asked him about that, and he said: 'Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, calculated the wealth and the poor, and He found what would suffice them to be twenty-five from every thousand, and if that had not sufficed them, He would have increased it for them.'

He said: So I returned to him and informed him, and he said, 'This question came on a camel from the Hijaz.' Then he said, 'If I were to give obedience to anyone, I would give it to the master of this speech.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ الْأَحْوَل: Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal (Mu'min al-Taq) — a famous Shia dialectical theologian and close companion of Imam al-Sadiq
key_terms.الزَّكَاة: Zakat — the obligatory alms-tax in Islam, 2.5% of qualifying wealth held for one year
key_terms.الزَّنَادِقَة: Zanadiqa — atheists or freethinkers, particularly those who questioned divine legislation
key_terms.حَسَبَ: Calculated/computed — the Imam uses this word to convey that divine legislation is based on precise divine knowledge, not arbitrary decree

ai.seo_question: Why is the Islamic zakat rate set at 2.5% (twenty-five dirhams per thousand)?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a theological dispute about the divine wisdom behind the Zakat rate of 2.5% (25 dirhams per 1000). Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal, a renowned Shia debater, first gave an analogical answer to an atheist challenger, likening the seemingly arbitrary zakat rate to the varying number of prayer units (2, 3, and 4 rak'at). Later, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) revealed the true divine wisdom: God had actually calculated the total wealth and the total needs of the poor, and determined that 2.5% was precisely the amount that would suffice the poor. The atheist challenger's admiration of the Imam's reasoning — expressed through the saying about obedience — suggests even non-believers found the Imam's answer intellectually compelling.
word_analysis: He would have increased it for them

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Abu Ja’far Al Ahowl who said,

‘A man from the atheists asked me saying, ‘How come the Zakāt came to be twenty five from every thousand Dirhams?’ So I said to him, ‘But rather that is like the Salāt, being of three (Cycles), and two (Cycles) and four (Cycles) (i.e., an arbitrary number)’. So he accepted it from me.

Then I met Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> after that. So I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about that, and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Counted the wealth and the poor ones, so He<sup>azwj</sup> Found what would suffice them as being twenty five from every thousand, and if that would not have sufficed them, would have Increased (the proportion) for them.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I returned to him and informed him, and he said, ‘This question has come upon the camel from Al-Hijaz’. Then he said, ‘If I were to obey anyone obediently, I would obey the author of this speech’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus from abu Ja‘far al-Ahwal who has said the following:
“Once an atheist asked me, ‘Why is the amount of zakat twenty- five on every one thousand?’ I replied, ‘It is because Salah (prayer) is of two, three and four Rak‘at.’

He (the narrator) has said, ‘He agreed with me. I then visited abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked him about it.’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, calculated wealthy and destitute people. He found that twenty-five on every one thousand is enough. If this much did not suffice, He would have increased it.’
I went to the atheist and informed him about it. He said, ‘This answer has come from Hijaz on the back of camel.’ He then said, ‘Were I to obey anyone I would obey the author of this statement.’”
